title: Integral derived reduction detects isomorphisms
statement: For ℓ and finite normed E/ℚ_ℓ, use the coefficient rings and scalar functors of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Let X be any scheme with noetherian underlying space and M,N bounded constructible complexes of internal O_E coefficient modules. If derived reduction of a morphism φ:M→N along O_E→O_E/(ℓ) is invertible in the full residue derived category, then φ is invertible. No properness or exchange assumption is made.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), integral constructibility and derived Nakayama

proof.text: Apply integral constructible closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions. The source-library weak Serre criterion makes the bounded constructible property triangulated. A distinguished cone C of φ is consequently isomorphic to a bounded constructible object C'.

Derived extension of scalars is triangulated by its exact right adjoint. Since the reduced φ is invertible, the reduction of C is zero. Transport to C' and use the coefficient short exact sequence and K-flat tensor cone comparison to conclude that ℓ times its identity is invertible.

Every homology functor is additive, so ℓ acts invertibly on every cohomology module of C'. Each such module is constructible. Integral constructible Nakayama makes it zero; homology detects the zero derived object, hence C=0. The distinguished triangle makes φ.hom invertible, and the full subcategory reflects this to φ.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), integral constructibility and derived Nakayama
proof_origin.note: B4: use the coefficient short exact sequence to make ℓ invertible on the zero-reduction cone, then the proved internal constructible Nakayama theorem on every cohomology module. Integral Serre closure is proved from generic cokernel/extension closure and the sole remaining integral kernel hole. This avoids top-degree tensor comparison and descending bounded induction.
